topic: Root-cause trace for the gen2/gen1 --version and self-check SIGSEGV residual documented in artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_rodata_overflow_20260903.json -> residual_not_fixed_by_this (id: gen2-version-sigsegv-after-rodata-fix)
summary: Traced the crash (str_eq called with the raw ASCII bytes of an unrelated 8-byte string literal, "--output", sitting where a pointer argument should be) three call-frames deeper than the prior session's gdb work. Root cause: arg_list_get's compiled body reads the ArgList.len field from the WRONG byte offset (offset 384 / slot 48) instead of the correct location. The garbage value read as "len" is enormous, so the `i >= lst.len` bounds check never trips, and the function falls through to return whatever garbage sits at the mis-computed items[i] address -- which for this binary happens to be the raw bytes of the string literal "--output" used elsewhere in main.sio's argument-parsing code. This is a struct field-offset computation bug for structs containing a fixed-size array field ([string; 64]), not the string-literal codegen bug hypothesized in the prior session's audit.
method: gdb --batch on gen2_final.elf (the binary carrying BOTH the rc19/rc20 capacity fix and the rc23 rodata fix, still built without any of this session's diagnostic instrumentation) running `--version`.

break *<crash_addr> (0x37044bf) instead of letting SIGSEGV happen: this keeps the stack/registers intact for backward tracing via the return address at [rsp], rather than gdb's post-mortem unwinder (which fails immediately -- 'Cannot access memory' -- because the crash is on the routine's very first instruction, before any frame is set up).

Walked the call chain backward one frame at a time: crash site (str_eq-shaped byte-compare loop) -> caller at 0x344bad0 (compiler_mode_has_flag's compiled body, confirmed against source by matching the i<args.len loop-condition codegen, the arg_list_get call, and the str_eq call) -> its own caller of arg_list_get at 0x343236a.

Set a breakpoint at arg_list_get's entry (0x343236a) and captured RDI/RSI: RDI=0x7fff83e000f8 (a real, valid stack address -- the lst argument was passed correctly), RSI=0 (i=0, correct). Confirmed via `continue` that arg_list_get is called exactly ONCE before the crash (matches args.len effectively being 1 for `--version` alone) and returns straight into the crashing str_eq call -- i.e. the corruption originates INSIDE arg_list_get's own body, not in how it was called.

Dumped 80 qwords (640 bytes) of raw memory at the lst pointer (0x7fff83e000f8) to inspect the ArgList struct's actual on-stack layout, and cross-referenced against the field-offset immediate baked into arg_list_get's compiled bounds-check (`mov $0x30,%rbx; mov (%rax,%rbx,8),%rax` == read *(lst_ptr + 48*8) == *(lst_ptr + 384), then compared against `i` via setle to implement `i >= lst.len`).

findings.compiled_len_field_offset: 384 bytes (slot 48) from the ArgList base pointer, hardcoded as an immediate in arg_list_get's compiled body.
findings.memory_at_that_offset: 0x0000000003829858 -- a value in the same numeric family as this binary's own CODE addresses (crash site was 0x37044bf, caller was 0x344bad0/0x343236a, all in the 0x3xxxxxx range), and part of a long unbroken run of CONSECUTIVE ascending values (0x3829833, 0x3829834, ... 0x3829871, i.e. 63 back-to-back 8-byte slots each exactly 1 greater than the last) spanning stack offsets 0x58 through 0x340. This is not real ArgList data -- it looks like stale/uninitialized stack content (plausibly a leftover label-patch table, address table, or similar sequential structure from an earlier, unrelated call on the same stack region) that get_args() never actually wrote over for slots beyond the few it populated.
findings.where_the_real_data_actually_is: The struct's first ~9 slots (offset 0-0x48) hold small, plausible-looking values (255, 16, 0, 0, 1, 1, 255, 512, 64, 1 across offsets 0-0x48). Offset 0x50 (slot 10) holds 0x7fffffffeb94 -- a real, live stack address, almost certainly the actual pointer to the argv string content ("--version") that get_args() wrote. This is a strong signal that the field currently read as 'len' at slot 48 is not just wrong in isolation -- the compiler's own field-offset math for this struct disagrees with where the constructing code (get_args(), building the struct via `lst.items[i] = get_arg(i)` and `lst.len = n`) actually placed the data.
why_this_explains_the_full_crash_chain: 1. The garbage read as ArgList.len (0x3829858, tens of millions) makes the `i >= lst.len` bounds check in arg_list_get() effectively never trip for small i.

2. arg_list_get falls through to `lst.items[i as usize]` using -- per the same offset-computation logic that produced 384 for .len -- an equally miscomputed address for items[0], landing on unrelated stack/data content: specifically the raw 8-byte packed ASCII content of the string literal "--output" (which appears elsewhere in main.sio's real argument-parsing code, e.g. for a -o/--output flag), rather than a pointer to the real args[0] string.

3. compiler_mode_has_flag's `arg_list_get(args, i) == needle` then calls str_eq(that_garbage_value, needle), and str_eq's compiled body immediately dereferences its first argument as if it were a pointer (`movzbq (%rdi),%rax`) -- but %rdi holds "--output"'s raw bytes (0x74757074756f2d2d), not an address, so the read faults.

candidate_root_cause_in_source.location: self-hosted/ir/lower.sio, the struct-layout family of helpers (struct_layout_slot_count, struct_layout_field_pos, struct_layout_field_name_at) plus the native_v2 IrFieldGet codegen in self-hosted/native/codegen_x86_linux.sio (`field_idx + native_v2_object_header_size()/8`, header size = 32 bytes -> +4 words) that codegen_x86_linux.sio:9033-ish region consumes.
candidate_root_cause_in_source.documented_precedent: self-hosted/ir/lower.sio's own comments (near emit_struct_value_copy_deep, ~line 7660) explicitly flag that Madaros/native_v2 lays out a struct as ONE WORD PER FIELD with aggregate fields (arrays, nested structs) held as a separate HANDLE -- while lean_single (the bootstrap-stage compiler) INLINES aggregate fields (`struct_like_nslots = st_total_size / 8`), i.e. the TWO compiler generations disagree about struct layout for any struct containing an array field. The comment states outright: 'Making the two agree would touch struct-literal lowering, every field offset, the native backend and the SOIR wire layout' -- i.e. this is a KNOWN, ACKNOWLEDGED architectural inconsistency, not a new discovery. ArgList (`items: [string; 64], len: i64`) is exactly the shape this warning describes.
candidate_root_cause_in_source.ruled_out_but_close: native_v2_object_header_size() = 32 bytes (4 words). field_idx(len)=1 + 4 = 5, not 48 -- so the simple 'header + field_idx' formula does NOT by itself explain 48. struct_layout_slot_count's own field-registration walk (max registered `.index` + 1) would give len index 1 for a cleanly-registered 2-field ArgList, also not 48. The doc comment's warning about a struct type being registered TWICE (declaration pass + import/literal seeding) with `field_count` doubling is the strongest remaining lead: `pub struct ArgList` is used across get_args()/arg_list_get()/compiler_mode_has_flag() etc., all within main.sio, and if a duplicate/stale registration pollutes the layout table entry that `arg_list_get`'s codegen consults, a field index as high as 48 could plausibly result. This was NOT confirmed further -- it is the most promising lead for the next session to chase, e.g. by instrumenting struct_layout_field_pos/struct_layout_slot_count specifically for type_name=="ArgList" and printing every registration event plus the final registered field_count/indices.
candidate_root_cause_in_source.not_the_cause: self-hosted/native/codegen_x86_linux.sio:4676's native_v2_core_emit_str_eq_into (which hardcodes a second string argument at `arg0_reg + 1`, a real and separate calling-convention bug) is dead code from the standard main.sio compile path's perspective -- it is only wired into self-hosted/compiler/native_compile_driver.sio's builtin-emitter dispatch table, a separate/legacy bootstrap driver not exercised when gen1 compiles main.sio via the normal self-hosted/ir/lower.sio -> codegen_x86_linux.sio IrCall pipeline. Worth fixing on its own merits (real bug, wrong calling convention) but it is NOT reachable from the crash we traced, so it is a distinct, independently-discovered defect rather than the cause of this residual.

session_context.why_the_investigation_took_this_path: Attempting to add finer-grained print-based instrumentation directly inside compiler_mode_has_flag (to empirically bisect between arg_list_get vs the str_eq call as the corruption's origin) triggered a THIRD, independent, and much cheaper-to-reproduce bug: gen1 rebuilt from the edited main.sio segfaults on ITS OWN self-check (`run_check_mode: about to check 125 modules` immediately precedes the crash) before ever reaching gen2. Root-caused separately via gdb (RSP itself pointed at unmapped memory) as a genuine stack overflow: this codebase has many functions the compiler's own warnings already flag with absurd stack-frame sizes (tens of MB, some obviously-bogus multi-petabyte readings from a separate size-computation bug) due to widespread by-value struct/array parameter passing, and gen1's deep self-check recursion over a 40,000-line file exhausts the default 8 MiB stack (`ulimit -s`) that SSH/build scripts inherit. Confirmed fixed by `ulimit -s unlimited` before invoking gen1 (gen1 then progresses cleanly past the check phase into normal module lowering). Also confirmed this stack-overflow fix does NOT affect the original --version crash (gen2_final.elf --version still segfaults identically under `ulimit -s unlimited`), so the two are independent bugs -- the stack overflow is real and worth fixing (or at minimum documenting the ulimit requirement for gen1 self-checks of main.sio) but is not this residual.
session_context.gdb_technique_worth_recording: For a raw hand-written ELF with no section headers (`readelf -S` reports 'There are no sections in this file'), objdump -d --start-address=... produces no output at all -- gdb's `x/Ni <addr>` against a LIVE (running or breakpointed) process is the only disassembly path that works, since gdb resolves addresses through the process's actual memory mappings rather than static section metadata. Breaking BEFORE a fault (rather than examining post-mortem) is essential whenever the crash is at a function's very first instruction: the backtrace unwinder needs at least a saved frame pointer to walk, and a leaf/just-entered routine has none yet -- but the return address is still reliably sitting at [rsp] and can be read/disassembled directly.

status_at_time_of_writing: A confirmation build (gen1 rebuilt from source carrying granular DIAG:hf:entry/pre/got/match print checkpoints inside compiler_mode_has_flag, built under ulimit -s unlimited to route around the unrelated stack-overflow bug) was still in progress (self-compiling gen2, ~35% through module lowering) when this document was written. Its result -- confirming whether the crash lands specifically inside the arg_list_get call, the str_eq call, or the loop's own bookkeeping -- should be folded in as a follow-up once it completes; the gdb trace above already answers this more precisely than the checkpoints would (corruption is inside arg_list_get's own field-offset computation, confirmed via direct memory inspection), so the build's main remaining value is as an independent cross-check.
